How to Prevent Termites — Expert Tips for Homeowners

By Shaw's Pest Control  ·  Wichita, KS

How to Prevent Termites: A Homeowner's Guide to Protection

If you're searching for how to prevent termites, you're already ahead of most homeowners. Termite prevention isn't glamorous, but it's far easier—and cheaper—than dealing with an active infestation. In Kansas, where subterranean termites thrive in our clay-rich soil and humid summers, a few smart habits can make the difference between a protected home and thousands of dollars in structural damage. Shaw's Pest Control has been helping Wichita-area families since 1987, and our Master Tech-certified technicians have seen firsthand what works—and what homeowners overlook. This guide covers the prevention steps you can handle yourself, and where professional help makes sense.

Why Termites Target Your Home (And How to Make It Less Appealing)

Termites don't randomly pick houses to invade. They're drawn to three things: moisture, wood, and easy access. Subterranean termites—the species we deal with across Kansas—live in the soil and travel upward in search of cellulose (wood fiber). They build mud tubes to protect themselves as they move from the ground into your home's structure.

Your home becomes a target when conditions make survival easy. Leaky gutters create damp soil along your foundation. Mulch piled against siding gives termites a hidden pathway. Crawl spaces with poor ventilation turn into humid breeding grounds. The good news? Most of these risk factors are within your control. Termites need consistent moisture to survive, so eliminating water sources around your foundation is the single most effective prevention step you can take. Fix downspouts that dump water too close to the house, repair leaking faucets or AC units, and grade your soil so water flows away from the foundation—not toward it.

Practical Steps to Reduce Termite Risk Around Your Property

Prevention starts outside. Walk the perimeter of your home and look for direct wood-to-soil contact. Wooden deck posts, fence boards, or siding that touches the ground creates a termite highway. Use concrete footers for deck posts and maintain at least six inches of clearance between soil and any wood siding or framing.

Next, reconsider your mulch. Mulch retains moisture and provides cover—exactly what termites need. Keep mulch at least 12 inches away from your foundation, and consider switching to gravel or rock in high-risk areas near the house. If you store firewood, keep it elevated off the ground and at least 20 feet from the structure. Termites will colonize a woodpile, and once they're established, they'll start exploring nearby buildings.

Check your gutters and downspouts twice a year. Clogged gutters overflow onto fascia boards and saturate the soil below, creating perfect conditions for termite activity. Extend downspouts so they release water at least four feet from the foundation. Inside your home, inspect crawl spaces and basements for standing water, condensation on pipes, or musty odors—all signs of excess moisture that termites exploit.

Ventilate crawl spaces properly. Install vents that allow airflow and consider a vapor barrier over exposed soil. Termites thrive in still, humid environments, and a well-ventilated crawl space disrupts their preferred conditions.

When DIY Prevention Isn't Enough—And What to Do About It

Even with perfect maintenance, termites can still find a way in. That's because they're underground, often moving through cracks in your foundation that you can't see or seal yourself. This is where professional termite control makes the difference. Chemical barriers applied around your foundation create a treated zone that kills termites on contact or prevents them from crossing. These treatments last for years and protect areas you can't manage with a rake or a gutter scoop.

Annual termite inspections are the smartest investment a homeowner can make. Shaw's Pest Control offers thorough inspections that check not just the visible signs, but the hidden risk zones—crawl spaces, pier-and-beam areas, expansion joints, and foundation cracks. Our technicians hold three state certifications and Master Tech credentials, so we know what subtle warning signs look like before they become expensive problems.

If you're buying a home, selling one, or just haven't had an inspection in over a year, schedule one. Termite damage rarely announces itself until it's advanced. A professional can spot early signs—mud tubes, frass, hollow-sounding wood, or discarded wings—that homeowners typically miss. And if treatment is needed, acting early saves you thousands compared to waiting until the damage spreads. You can learn more about our termite inspection and treatment process here.

Termite Prevention in Wichita and Surrounding Areas

Wichita's clay soil and seasonal humidity make it prime termite territory. According to data from the Kansas Department of Agriculture, subterranean termites are active year-round in our region, though activity peaks in spring and early summer when swarmers emerge. Homes in Derby, El Dorado, Andover, and surrounding areas face the same risks—especially older homes with crawl spaces or slab foundations that have settled and cracked over time.

Local construction methods also play a role. Many homes built before the 1990s lack modern termite barriers or treated lumber. If your home was built during that era, it's worth having a baseline inspection even if you've never seen signs of termites. For homeowners in El Dorado dealing with older housing stock or properties near wooded areas, professional termite control services can provide targeted protection tailored to your home's specific vulnerabilities.

Frequently Asked Questions

What attracts termites to a house?

Termites are attracted to moisture, wood, and soil contact. Homes with leaky gutters, poor drainage, mulch against the foundation, or wood touching the ground are at higher risk. They're also drawn to damp crawl spaces and areas with consistent humidity. Reducing moisture and eliminating wood-to-soil contact are the most effective ways to make your home less appealing.

How often should I inspect my home for termites?

You should have a professional termite inspection at least once a year. Homeowners should also conduct visual checks every few months—look for mud tubes along the foundation, discarded wings near windows, or soft, hollow-sounding wood. If you live in an older home or an area with known termite activity, increase the frequency to twice a year.

Can I prevent termites without chemicals?

Yes, to a degree. Reducing moisture, eliminating wood-to-soil contact, keeping mulch away from the foundation, and maintaining proper ventilation all help. However, physical prevention alone can't stop termites that are already in the soil around your home. Chemical barriers and professional treatments provide a defensive layer that DIY methods can't replicate.

Do termite barriers really work?

Yes. Professional liquid termiticide barriers create a treated zone in the soil around your foundation that either kills termites on contact or repels them. When applied correctly by a licensed technician, these barriers can last five to ten years and dramatically reduce the risk of infestation. They're especially effective for homes in high-risk areas.

What's the best mulch to avoid termites?

Gravel, rubber mulch, or cedar mulch are better options than traditional wood mulch. However, no mulch is termite-proof. The key is keeping any mulch material at least 12 inches away from your foundation and monitoring the area regularly. If you prefer wood mulch for aesthetics, just maintain distance and check for termite activity during your seasonal yard work.

Are termites active in winter in Kansas?

Subterranean termites remain active underground year-round in Kansas, even in winter. Cold temperatures slow their activity, but they don't hibernate. Termites inside your walls or in heated crawl spaces can continue feeding regardless of the outdoor temperature. This is why annual inspections shouldn't be skipped just because it's cold outside.

Ready to Protect Your Home From Termites?

Prevention is always easier than repair. Whether you're taking your first steps to reduce termite risk or you want a professional set of eyes on your property, Shaw's Pest Control is here to help. Since 1987, our family-run team has served Wichita and the surrounding communities with honest, no-pressure expertise. We'll inspect your home, explain what we find, and give you a clear plan—whether that's a few DIY fixes or a protective treatment.
